mechanism_narrative: Sustained upward trend in WORKPLACES mobility (rising from -17.7% to -10.9% over four weeks) signals normalization of commuting patterns. This drives weekday retail footfall recovery as workers resume in-person schedules, producing net positive RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES improved 6.8 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the prior 28 days, or WORKPLACES reverses by more than 3 percentage points in week t+1.

mechanism_narrative: Declining RESIDENTIAL mobility (from 14.0% to 11.7% over four weeks) indicates residents are spending less time at home, reallocating time to out-of-home activities. This reallocation directly increases RETAIL_REC visits as suppressed demand is released.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.3 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to its four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station mobility has improved consistently (from -30.9% to -24.7% over four weeks). When TRANSIT crosses above -25% threshold, it signals sufficient public transport capacity and user confidence to support retail district foot traffic, driving RETAIL_REC gains.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -24.7% in t-0w, above -25 threshold
failure_condition: TRANSIT falls below -26% in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in weeks t+1 and t+2 relative to t-0w baseline.

mechanism_narrative: Joint improvement in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility creates a reinforcing cycle: commuting recovery enables retail district accessibility, while transit capacity supports worker return. This interaction produces accelerated RETAIL_REC growth over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improve week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:both series show consistent improvement over four weeks
failure_condition: Either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT reverses by more than 2 percentage points in week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not exceed prior four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains suppressed (declining from -10.6% to -8.3%) while RETAIL_REC shows marginal improvement. This divergence indicates outdoor recreation is not substituting for retail; instead, retail recovery is driven by necessity-based shopping (GROCERY_PHARM stable near -5%), suggesting discretionary retail will lag.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -8% and GROCERY_PHARM stays within -3% to -7%
failure_condition: PARKS mobility rises above -5% in week t+1, or GROCERY_PHARM falls below -8%, indicating shift to discretionary spending.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved 6.2 percentage points over four weeks, approaching pre-restriction levels. If TRANSIT crosses -20% threshold in the next week, it signals policy-driven capacity expansion or restriction relaxation, triggering retail district reopenings and RETAIL_REC acceleration.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved 6.2 points from t-3w to t-0w
failure_condition: TRANSIT does not exceed -20% by week t+1, or RETAIL_REC does not increase in week t+1 relative to t-0w.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved 3.4 percentage points over four weeks (from -23.7% to -20.3%), establishing a consistent upward trend independent of other mobility categories. This trend continuation mechanism predicts RETAIL_REC will continue improving at similar rate over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.4 percentage points over four weeks at consistent rate
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines in week t+1 relative to t-0w, or the four-week mean of RETAIL_REC does not exceed -20.3%.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility decline combined with WORKPLACES recovery indicates a shift from home-based to work-based and out-of-home activity. However, GROCERY_PHARM remains depressed, signaling consumers are not yet confident in discretionary spending. RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed as essential shopping dominates.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines while WORKPLACES rises and GROCERY_PHARM stays below -4%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rises above -2% in week t+1, indicating confidence recovery, or RETAIL_REC exceeds prior four-week mean.
